review_reference: Backend plan, Part 3 "Item 5" (written as 0108), and the owner's decisions recorded there: D10 "send the campaign name now" and D11 "linking an outreach case by Health ID works only when the worker already has access to that patient". The number 0115 assigned by the coordinator (0106-0114 belong to other builders). Unsigned until the owner signs.
evidence: In plain words, applying 0115 to production does this. It adds two new Outreach tables and two name readers and changes nothing that exists. Field officers can record a visit, referral or follow-up on a registration (outreach.registration_case_visits); only staff who may already read that registration at that clinic, and for a campaign registration only members of that campaign, can read or add them, and nobody can change or delete one. A small log (outreach.link_preview_attempts) holds only ids and a time for each Health ID check, so outreach-api can stop a member after 20 checks an hour; it never holds the Health ID. Two readers give the staff name (and nothing else) of the person who registered a case, and of campaign members who share a campaign with the caller, at the caller's clinic only, at most 200 at a time, without locking any row. The Outreach runtime gets read and insert on the two tables and may run the two readers, in the migration (for roles that already exist) and in runtime-grants.sql (its 0115 block), identically; nothing is granted to PUBLIC. Nothing is used until outreach-api's OUTREACH_VISITS_ENABLED is turned on; today's image calls none of it. Locks, measured with pg_locks before commit on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 copy migrated through 0105 by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on outreach.registration_cases and identity.staff_facility_memberships (the new foreign keys), taken NOWAIT every 10 ms for at most 5 seconds; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the new tables and their indexes; the catalogs' own locks; no other application table. The whole apply took 7 ms; with a writer holding outreach.registration_cases it stopped after 5.1 s with 55P03 and applied nothing. Proof: the suite services/ehr-api/test/database/outreach-visits.integration.sql (59 cases) passes on a fresh superuser-migrated database (readers lent to an owner without BYPASSRLS) and on an upgrade from 0105 in production shape (owner hid_migrator, NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS).
